worked: Federal AGI = wages (person 0) 245,050.00 = 245,050.00. Federal taxable income = 245,050.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 229,300.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Illinois starts from federal AGI). Form IL-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 245,050.00. Line 2 federally tax-exempt interest 10,000.00. Line 3 other additions 0.00. Line 4 = 255,050.00. Line 5 0.00. Lines 6 and 7 0.00. Line 8 = 0.00. Line 9 base income = 255,050.00 - 0.00 = 255,050.00. Income Exceptions: federal AGI 245,050.00 is not greater than 250,000.00, so the allowance stands. Line 10a 2,850.00. Line 10b 0.00. Lines 10c and 10d 0.00. Line 10 = 2,850.00. Line 11 net income = 255,050.00 - 2,850.00 = 252,200.00. Line 12 tax = 252,200.00 x 4.95% = 12,483.9000. The form takes whole dollars only and would show 12,484.00; expected uses the formula to the cent. Lines 13-18 0.00 (no credits in the projection). Line 19 state income tax = 12,483.90. Line 4 is over 250,000.00, but the test reads federal AGI, which is 245,050.00, so the allowance stands.
accepted_approximations: All municipal bond interest is taxed. Illinois adds back all federally tax-exempt interest and exempts only listed obligations (Schedule M Lines 34 and 35), which a projection cannot tell from others.
